full_judgment:
9. In the supplementary affidavit it is stated that similar question of fact raised in the Title Suit No. 383 of 1983 (re-numbered as Title Suit No. 83 of 1985) filed by the alleged purchasers Abdul Khaleque Munshi and 9 others as plaintiffs against the Government of Bangladesh represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka and others for declarations of title is pending in the Court of First Subordinate Judge, Dhaka. Same questions of facts have also been raised in another suit being Title Suit No. 217 of 1989 filed by the M/s. Capital Property Limited against the Government was declared and the appeal against the judgment and decree being Title Appeal No.380 of 1990 is pending in the First Commercial Court (Subordinate Judge), Dhaka wherein the appellant, Government has obtained an order of stay of operation of the judgment and decree of trial Court. It is also stated that Title Suit No.129 of 1995 filed by Abdul Khaleque Munshi was decreed ex parte. The suit was filed by Abdul Khaleque, the predecessor of the petitioners suppressing the judgment passed in SA No.685 of 1970 of the High Court Division and that subsequently in CP No. 84 of 1974 the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court affirmed the said judgment of the High Court Division. In the said judgment the petitioner's predecessor Abdul Khaleque Munshi and others were declared as mere bargaders in respect of the suit Plot No. 565 and it was held that they had not acquired tenancy right under the Bhawal Court of Wards Estate. he land in CS Plot No. 565 was acquired by the Government from the then DIT as khas land of the Government and the compensation assessed therefor was deposited in the Government fund in LR Head No. 7 (Photocopy of Judgment in SA No.685 of 1970 by the High Court Division and the photo copy judgment in CP No. 84 of 1974 by the High Co Division are Annexures 1 and 2 respectively). Abdul Khaleque Munshi obtained the ex parte decree in Title Suit No. 125 of 1975 suppressing the judgment passed in CP No. 84 of 1974, DIT had no authority to come to a mutual settlement. Sections 92 and 93 of Town Improvement Act empowers DIT to relinquish its claim only when the possession of the property is not taken over and Gazette notification is not published. After delivery of possession and Gazette notification, Deputy Commissioner is the only authority to handle the acquired property as an authorised agent of the Government. The petitioner's predecessors by playing fraud upon the DIT managed the execution and registration of agreement (Annexure-A) which is not binding upon the Government. It is submitted that a number of Civil suits filed by both the parties are pending in different civil Courts and the petitioner's predecessors have also taken recourse to the alternative remedy by way of filing suits and the questions at issue in the said civil suits are essentially the same as that of the present Writ petitions remedy under section 102 is not available. The petitioners knowing full well about the fraud of their predecessors have purchased the parcels of land in dispute and so they are parties to the fraud and that being so, neither the petitioner nor their predecessors, had any right, title, interest and possession in the suit plot which is the khas land of the Government. The Government has legally published the notice in the newspaper in which the name of Capital Property Ltd. was mentioned and, as such, the petitioner has no locus standi to file this petition. In the further supplementary affidavit filed on behalf of the Respondent No. 1 the photo copy of the judgment and decree of Title Suit No. 89 of 1982, judgment of SA No. 347 of 1965 have been annexed as Annexure-3-3(a) and 3(b) respectively. 

 18. Mr. Moinul Hoque, the learned Senior Counsel appearing for the respondent No. 4 Managing Director Jalal Housing Ltd, joined his voice with the petitioners in challenging the notice published on 10-7-89 in the Daily Inqilab vide Annexure-C to the petition but his manner of attack is slightly different from that of the petitioners counsel Mr. KS Nabi. In the affidavit filed on behalf of the respondent No.4 it is stated that the Capital Properties Ltd. has stepped into the shoes of M/s, Shah Jalal Housing Ltd. It is stated that out of the entire land only 27.89 acres were shown as khas and compensation was paid therefor. In the supplementary affidavit filed on behalf of respondent No. 4 the photocopy of the possession paper has been annexed with its map as Annexure I and the report of the Review Committee have been filed. From the report it appears that the question as to how much land of plot No.565 was Khas and how much was privately owned could not be determined otherwise than by a civil suit. In the further affidavit filed on behalf of the respondent No. 4 on 16-2-95 the judgment and decree of TS 89/62 passed by the 1st Subordinate Judge, Dhaka has been annexed. The suit filed against Abdul Khaleque was dismissed on 30-3-64. Title Appeal No. 134 of 1964 filled by Abdul Khaleque and others was dismissed by the same judgment by the Additional District Judge, 1st Court Dhaka. Thus from the lengthy argument of Mr. Moinul Hoque it boils down that the land which was acquired by the Government at the instance of RAJUK was not the khas land of the Government and the acquisition in LA case was declared invalid by the decree of the 4th Sub-Judge Dhaka passed in TS No.129/75 on 24-7-76. The ex parte decree was upheld on appeal on 14-2-84 and hence practically there was no acquisition (5 DLR 81 relevant 84 void ab initio) under section 27 of the Bengal Tenancy Act and under section 27 of the State Acquisition Act has been referred in support of his contention.
